headline: Parks Canada Admission for the Viking National Historic Site
reservation: While site entry usually does not require advance booking for individuals, guided tours and special programs may have limited capacity. Verify operational dates as the site is strictly seasonal, typically closing for the winter; check the Parks Canada site for the current year's schedule.

days.title: Viking Archaeology and Sod Huts

stops.name: Norse Reconstrution Buildings
stops.detail: Step inside recreated sod houses to experience the daily life of Leif Erikson’s 11th-century expedition.

stops.name: The Archaeological Site
stops.detail: View the original excavated remains of the Norse settlement, now a UNESCO World Heritage site.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from St. Anthony; the road is paved but narrow in sections.
days.note: Coastal winds can be high; the site is primarily outdoors with limited indoor shelter between buildings.

days.title: Coastal Barrens and Iceberg Viewing

stops.name: Birchy Noddle Hill Trail
stops.detail: Climb the boardwalk for a panoramic view of the site, the surrounding barrens, and the Sacred Bay.

stops.name: Skinners Cove
stops.detail: Walk the rugged coastline to look for icebergs drifting south during the early summer months.

days.driving: Allow 15-20 minutes from local accommodations; watch for moose on the roads at dawn and dusk.
days.note: Iceberg sightings are highly seasonal and dependent on ocean currents; check local trackers.

days.title: Regional Maritime History
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from the Visitor Centre

stops.name: Visitor Centre Exhibits
stops.detail: Examine authentic Norse artifacts recovered from the site and watch the introductory film.

stops.name: Norstead
stops.detail: Visit the nearby non-government merchant outpost recreation to see a full-scale Viking ship replica.

days.driving: Allow 10 minutes between the Historic Site and Norstead; local transfers are short.
days.note: Norstead is a separate attraction from the National Historic Site; separate admission may apply.

intel.title: Visitor Lot
intel.text: The main parking area at the Visitor Centre is sufficient for most daily visitors but can feel crowded during tour bus arrivals. Arriving at opening or late afternoon provides a quieter experience.

intel.title: Remote Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is weak and unreliable throughout the Great Northern Peninsula. Download all maps and travel documents before leaving the Deer Lake or St. Anthony airport areas.

intel.title: Great Northern Fuel
intel.text: St. Anthony is the primary hub for fuel, groceries, and mechanical services. Ensure your tank is sufficient for the return trip as options in Griquet are very limited.

intel.title: Seasonal Window
intel.text: The site typically operates from June through September. Outside of these months, most facilities, including the visitor centre and reconstructions, are closed to the public.

intel.title: Walking Surfaces
intel.text: The site features gravel paths and wooden boardwalks. While designed for accessibility, the coastal winds and damp conditions can make outdoor movement challenging for some.

plan.arrival: Fly into St. Anthony (YAY), pick up a rental car, and head to St. Anthony for supplies. It is a 30-40 minute drive north to the historic site area.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for the Viking Trail (Highway 430); check rental contracts for restrictions on gravel side roads.
plan.goldenHour: Birchy Noddle Hill for sunset views over the Labrador Sea, subject to clear weather.
